name: Log Analytics Platform (ELK Stack)
description: Design a scalable log analytics platform similar to Datadog or Splunk. Covers log ingestion from distributed services, stream processing, full-text search indexing, time-series metrics extraction, and long-term storage.

learnSteps.title: High-Throughput Log Ingestion
learnSteps.description: 500+ application servers emit structured JSON logs via sidecar agents (Filebeat/Fluentd). Logs are published to Kafka partitioned by service name, enabling per-service ordering. With 128 partitions and 3x replication, the queue handles millions of log events per second. Kafka acts as a buffer during traffic spikes, decoupling producers from downstream processing speed. Back-pressure is handled at the agent level with local disk buffering.

learnSteps.title: Stream Processing and Enrichment
learnSteps.description: Flink consumes from Kafka, parsing raw log lines (regex/grok patterns), enriching with metadata (service name, datacenter, trace ID), and filtering noise (health checks, debug logs). It also extracts numeric metrics (response times, error counts) from logs in real-time. The at-least-once guarantee with idempotent sinks ensures no logs are lost. Parallelism of 64 matches the number of Kafka consumer partitions for maximum throughput.

learnSteps.title: Search Indexing and Querying
learnSteps.description: Enriched logs are bulk-indexed into Elasticsearch using time-based indices (logs-2024-01-15). Each index is sharded across 40 nodes for parallel indexing and search. Hot indices (last 24h) use SSDs for fast queries; warm indices (7-30 days) move to cheaper storage. Elasticsearch enables full-text search across billions of log entries with sub-second query latency using inverted indices. Index lifecycle management (ILM) automates rollover and deletion.

learnSteps.title: Metrics Extraction and Cold Storage
learnSteps.description: The Stream Processor extracts time-series metrics (error rate, p99 latency, request count) from logs and writes to InfluxDB with automatic downsampling (1-minute, 5-minute, 1-hour aggregations). This enables dashboards and alerting without querying raw logs. Raw logs older than 30 days are archived to S3 as compressed Parquet files for compliance and forensics. This tiered architecture keeps hot-path costs manageable while retaining years of data.

chaosScenarios.name: Incident-Driven Log Storm
chaosScenarios.description: An outage in the monitored fleet triggers 20x log volume — error storms with stack traces — exactly when engineers need the platform most
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Kafka absorbs the surge initially. Flink lag grows; Elasticsearch starts rejecting bulk indexing (es_rejected_execution). Ingest-to-searchable delay stretches from seconds to minutes during the very incident being debugged.
mitigationSteps: Enable DEBUG/INFO sampling at the agents for the noisiest services
Prioritize ERROR/WARN lanes through the pipeline
Raise the ES refresh interval to 30s to trade freshness for indexing throughput
Scale indexing-tier capacity and confirm the Kafka backlog drains

chaosScenarios.name: Elasticsearch Data Node Loss
chaosScenarios.description: A data node crashes, dropping shard copies and triggering a recovery/relocation storm
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Cluster goes yellow (red if any primary had no replica). Shard recovery I/O competes with live indexing; bulk rejections back-pressure Flink and Kafka lag grows. Queries on affected indices return partial results or fail.
mitigationSteps: Verify replicas were promoted and identify any red indices
Throttle shard recovery/relocation bandwidth to protect indexing
Delay index allocation if the node may return shortly (avoid pointless rebalancing)
Restore any lost indices from snapshot and replay the gap from Kafka

chaosScenarios.name: Poison Log Line Crash Loop
chaosScenarios.description: A malformed multiline log record crash-loops the Flink parsing stage, halting the entire pipeline
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: All three sinks (search, metrics, archive) stall simultaneously while producers are unaffected — Kafka lag grows linearly. Classic poison-pill signature: job restarts, hits the same record, dies again.
mitigationSteps: Identify the failing record from the task manager exception
Route it to the dead-letter queue and deploy a parser guard
Verify lag drains and spot-check the DLQ for related records

bottleneckProgression.description: Grok/regex parsing and enrichment saturate Flink CPU — parsing is the hidden hot loop of log pipelines
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale task managers, pre-compile patterns, push structured logging to the agents to skip parsing

bottleneckProgression.description: Elasticsearch indexing throughput hits the segment-merge I/O ceiling on hot data nodes
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add hot-tier data nodes, raise refresh interval, tune merge policy, adopt hot-warm ILM tiers

bottleneckProgression.description: Kafka broker network saturates from raw log throughput plus consumer fan-out
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add brokers, enable zstd compression at producers, rebalance partitions

expectedIssues.title: Dynamic Mapping Explosion
expectedIssues.description: Unstructured JSON logs with arbitrary field names blow past ES field limits and bloat cluster state
expectedIssues.mitigation: Strict index templates, flattened field types, total-field limits, reject unknown fields to a quarantine index

expectedIssues.title: Hot Shard Skew on Daily Indices
expectedIssues.description: Date-based index patterns route all of today's writes to a handful of shards while older shards idle
expectedIssues.mitigation: Size-based rollover via ILM, shard counts matched to hot-tier node count

expectedIssues.title: Searchable Retention Cost Bloat
expectedIssues.description: Keeping 90 days hot-searchable multiplies storage cost; most queries only touch the last 24-48 hours
expectedIssues.mitigation: Hot-warm-cold ILM with searchable snapshots in S3; accept slower queries on old data

expectedIssues.title: Pipeline Outage Exceeds Kafka Retention
expectedIssues.description: If indexing stays down longer than topic retention, logs are lost permanently — an audit/compliance risk
expectedIssues.mitigation: 72h retention with tiered storage; alert when lag exceeds 50% of the retention window

expectedIssues.title: Unbounded Wildcard Queries
expectedIssues.description: Leading-wildcard and wide-range dashboard queries starve indexing CPU on shared data nodes
expectedIssues.mitigation: Search circuit breakers, async search for long scans, dedicated coordinator nodes, query timeout policy

components.label: Search Engine (Elasticsearch)
components.costDriver: Hot + warm data nodes — dominant cost of the platform

slaDefinitions.name: Ingest-to-Searchable
slaDefinitions.penalty: Internal SLO — error budget burn blocks pipeline changes

metrics.name: consumer_lag
metrics.description: Kafka lag for the indexing consumer group

steps: Identify the noisiest services from Kafka topic metrics
Enable DEBUG/INFO sampling at their agents
Raise ES refresh interval to 30s and scale the indexing tier
Confirm bulk rejections stop and the Kafka backlog drains
List red indices and unassigned shards; identify the failed node
Restore replicas (restart node or allocate to peers) with throttled recovery
Restore irrecoverable indices from the latest snapshot
Replay the indexing gap from Kafka and verify document counts

runbooks.incident: Pipeline crash loop on poison record
steps: Pull the failing record from the task manager exception trace
Add a parser guard / route to dead-letter queue and redeploy
Restart the job from the last checkpoint
Verify lag drains and audit the DLQ for similar records

decisions.title: Kafka Buffer Between Producers and Indexing
decisions.context: Log volume spikes correlate exactly with incidents — the worst possible moment for the pipeline to shed data
decisions.decision: All agents write to Kafka; nothing downstream can block or slow a producer
consequences: Producers are isolated from Elasticsearch health entirely
A replay window exists for reprocessing after parser fixes
Topic retention defines the data-loss boundary and must be monitored against lag

decisions.title: Parse Once, Fork to Three Sinks
decisions.context: Search, dashboard metrics, and archival all need the same parsed events but with different stores
decisions.decision: A single Flink pipeline parses and enriches, then writes to Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, and S3
consequences: One consistent parsing path — no drift between search and metrics
S3 raw archive is the durable source of truth; Elasticsearch is a rebuildable view
The pipeline becomes a single point of processing failure, mitigated by checkpoints and the DLQ

decisions.title: Extract Metrics From Logs Into a TSDB
decisions.context: Dashboards refreshing aggregations against Elasticsearch are 10-100x more expensive than reading precomputed series
decisions.decision: Flink derives counters and latency histograms at ingest time and writes them to InfluxDB
consequences: Dashboards are cheap and fast, independent of search-cluster load
Metric definitions live in pipeline code and require deployment to change
Cardinality discipline is needed on extracted label sets

tradeoffs.choice: Tunable ES refresh interval (1s normal, 30s under pressure)
tradeoffs.benefit: Indexing throughput headroom exactly when log storms hit
tradeoffs.cost: Logs appear in search up to 30s late during incidents

tradeoffs.choice: Hot-warm-cold ILM with old data in S3 snapshots
tradeoffs.benefit: Storage cost scales with query value — recent data fast, old data cheap
tradeoffs.cost: Queries over old data require snapshot mounts and run far slower

alternatives.name: Agents Direct to Elasticsearch
alternatives.description: Filebeat-style shippers writing straight into ES ingest pipelines
alternatives.prosVsCons: Far fewer moving parts, but log storms hit the cluster unbuffered and parsing consumes data-node CPU
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Ingest spikes coincide with incidents; an unbuffered pipeline fails exactly when it is needed

alternatives.name: Columnar Store for Logs (ClickHouse-style)
alternatives.description: Store structured logs in a columnar OLAP database with SQL queries
alternatives.prosVsCons: Cheaper storage and fast aggregations, but weaker full-text relevance scoring and a thinner log-tooling ecosystem
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Free-text incident search is the primary workload; inverted indices fit it best

alternatives.name: Query Raw Archive Directly (Athena-style)
alternatives.description: Skip the search cluster; scan compressed S3 objects on demand
alternatives.prosVsCons: Cheapest possible storage with zero cluster ops, but queries take minutes
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Minutes-latency search is unusable for live incident response
